content: Insecticides are applied to target insects that come into contact with treated surfaces. For specific areas such as the flight deck, cockpit, and crew rest areas, a 2% permethrin aerosol is used instead of a residual treatment with 2% permethrin EC. When applied correctly, the permethrin 2% EC deposits on internal aircraft surfaces, such as cargo areas and passenger cabins, remain effective for up to 8 weeks. It is critical to follow the instructions on the product label for proper application. Equipment used for residual treatment must comply with WHO guidelines for vector control equipment, as outlined in the second edition of the 2018 WHO specifications. WHO also encourages the development of alternative residual treatment methods with proven efficacy. The discharge volume of the equipment should not exceed 10 mL/m² to prevent liquid runoff and surface wetting. The spray equipment must produce droplets with a volume median diameter (Dv) of at least 50 μm, and no more than 10% of droplets should be smaller than 30 μm to minimize the risk of inhalation. Battery-operated sprayers and ultra-low volume cold foggers are commonly used for aircraft disinsection. Electrostatic sprayers, which generate charged spray droplets for better coverage, are also effective but are primarily used for disinfection rather than disinsection. Pesticide products, including spray cans, must meet regulatory requirements approved by national pesticide registration authorities or WHO specifications. Airlines must comply with regulations in both the departure and arrival countries and may require additional testing to meet aircraft manufacturer specifications. Public health and aviation authorities should anticipate regulatory changes that may affect the use of chemicals in different jurisdictions. Airlines are responsible for notifying passengers and cargo customers about disinsection requirements during booking. Countries should provide clear information to airlines for dissemination to passengers and crew, explaining the national regulations, reasons for disinsection, and the safety of properly conducted procedures. Used aerosol containers must be stored and disposed of according to national regulations. On arrival, authorities may require that all exterior doors and windows, including cargo hold doors, remain closed until clearance is granted. Pre-embarkation cabin disinsection involves aerosol spraying of the aircraft cabin before passengers board. This method kills insects present at the time of disinsection and leaves a minimal but effective residue to kill insects that may board before departure. The procedure must be conducted after cleaning and drying of surfaces and after the aircraft has been fully catered, with service doors closed. Overhead and sidewall lockers should remain open during spraying, and the spray should be directed toward open lockers and the ceiling. Pre-departure cabin disinsection is an alternative to pre-embarkation treatment and is conducted after passengers have boarded and are seated, with all service doors closed. The procedure involves spraying all areas of the cabin, including the flight deck, open overhead lockers, and toilets. The aircraft’s air-conditioning must be switched off or set to normal flow during and for 5 minutes after spraying. Cargo holds also undergo disinsection. If residual spray treatment has not been completed, pre-departure cargo hold disinsection must be performed manually after all cargo has been loaded and just before the cargo hold door is closed. Sensitive electronic equipment must not be directly sprayed, and the crew must be informed of the procedure. For freighter aircraft, disinsection of the cargo area on the main deck should be conducted via the passenger access door after the large cargo door is closed. Aerosols should be discharged while walking away from the spray, and the area should be vacated once spraying is complete. If access to certain parts of the aircraft is restricted due to cargo, aerosols should be discharged into the center of the aircraft, directed toward the ceiling above the cargo. Used aerosol containers must remain in the cargo hold and be retrieved by ground handlers at the destination airport. If an airline chooses to remove aerosol containers before departure, they must be carried on board with the disinsection certificate. Any non-compliance with procedures must be reported to the intended first port before arrival. For cargo holds containing small animals, disinsection must be conducted before the animals are loaded but after all other cargo is on board. After activating aerosols, allow 7 minutes before loading animals.
